look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · UNARMED green black nightshade with ovate ALTERNATE leaves and WHITE flowers. Most distinctive: an apparently UNEVEN inflorescence (one branch with several flowers, another seeming to carry a single basal flower); anthers medium-length ~1.8–2.5 mm. DEVELOPING fruit has relatively long RECTANGULAR/OBLONG GREEN CALYX lobes with ROUNDED tips. Fully ripe berries commonly 10–14 mm wide and shiny BLACK. This is primarily a GREAT PLAINS species; a similar Hays County plant is not automatically S. interius. Confirm with reproductive detail or hold as Solanum morelloid complex.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Solanaceae: leaves alternate, flowers with joined usually 5-part corolla, 5 pollen-producing anthers, berry fruit. Unarmed morelloids distinguished from the larger prickly Solanum.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Unarmed green herb or short-lived subwoody perennial to around 1 m; base branching; broad ovate, simple alternate leaves, margins entire or shallowly toothed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: White five-lobed star-shaped corolla; projecting yellow anthers roughly 1.8–2.5 mm long, longer than S. emulans (1.5–1.8 mm in 2019 revision).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: UNEVEN-LOOKING inflorescence: a cluster of several flowers and a separate solitary-looking basal flower that is actually differently articulated on a pedicel.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Green calyx lobes relatively LONG, rectangular-to-oblong, apices rounded, particularly clear in developing fruit (photograph 3).

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Berries generally mature to glossy purplish-black; around 10–14 mm in diameter (larger than emulans ~6–8 mm); black gloss alone not species-diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Seeds typically ~1.8–2.0 mm; often only 2–4 hardened stone cells per ripe berry. Compare nigrescens 1.2–1.5 mm seeds and >6 stone cells.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Photos A–C are research field collections Nee 61350, and D is RBGE cultivated material; none is proof of a Hays County occurrence.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Branching green or slightly straw-colored herb, annual to somewhat persistent under trees; the 2019 revision emphasizes low-forest/shaded and open sand-hill habitats over the Great Plains. Leaf/plant height alone weakly diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Simple alternate green ovate-broadly ovate leaves, commonly about 4.5–11.2 × 2.3–6.8 cm in revision; wavy to shallowly toothed margins; hairs variable. Do not use leaf holes or pale shade as a species ID character.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: White five-lobed rotate/stellate corollas with yellow anthers approximately 1.8–2.5 mm long. Watch UNEVEN cluster arrangement and the articulation of its solitary-looking basal pedicel (about one-quarter to one-third its length upward according to revision). A hand lens and metric scale are recommended.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Round berries GREEN when immature then BLACK and approximately 10–14 mm at maturity. Calyx lobes are relatively long, rectangular, rounded-tipped; in mature fruit the green calyx persists under berry. Figure 22D depicts genuine mature black berries, whereas C is developing fruits. 2–4 sclerotic granules and larger seeds are advanced confirmatory characters.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: The 2019 monograph calls this primarily a Great Plains nightshade, in open sand hills and shaded low forest/under trees; Texas statewide documented, Hays County local applicability unresolved.

key_traits.label: Management
key_traits.text: Not a food-identification card. Do not eat berries or leaves; Morelloid nightshade taxonomy is difficult and plants can contain toxic alkaloids. When unsure, photograph flower/anthers, flowering-axis branching and mature fruit/green calyx together.

lookalikes.differences: Main key is an UNEVEN inflorescence with distinctive basal pedicel, medium anthers, long rounded-tip calyx, larger black berries. Multiple structures, never one character alone.

source_credit: Existing Hays Botany species record and scientific source notes; original full record retained in assigned family staging branch
